questions.question: Why is it safe for the planner's Dijkstra to stop when the target city is popped from the heap?
options: The heap is ordered by city name
The road graph is a tree
With non-negative weights, a node's distance is final the first time it is popped
Dijkstra pops every node exactly once anyway
questions.explanation: Non-negative edge weights guarantee no later path can be shorter than the one at the top of the min-heap.

questions.question: What does `if (d > dist.get(city)) continue;` do in fastestRoute?
options: Skips stale heap entries left behind after a shorter distance was found
Stops the search at the target
Prevents revisiting only the start city
questions.explanation: The heap is not updated in place; outdated entries remain and are skipped when popped (lazy deletion).

questions.question: For the 100 kg van, why does greedy (highest ₹ per kg first) earn less than DP?
options: DP is allowed to split parcels
Greedy sorts in ascending order of ratio
After P6, P2 and P4 (75 kg), nothing else fits the remaining 25 kg, while DP fills 100 kg with P1, P2 and P4
questions.explanation: Parcels are indivisible (0/1 knapsack), so locally best ratios can waste capacity; DP considers all combinations and earns ₹4,800 against ₹3,900.

questions.question: When does depotNetwork return null?
options: When two lanes have the same cost
When the candidate lanes cannot connect every depot (fewer than V - 1 lanes chosen)
When the input lanes contain a cycle
questions.explanation: A spanning tree on V depots needs exactly V - 1 edges; fewer means some depot is left disconnected.
